extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students studying algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, properties, and geometric interpretations of the module/sheaf of Kähler differentials (cotangent sheaf), conormal/normal sheaves, and the relative/tangent exact sequences for morphisms of schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential map axioms (da)
rubrics_metrics.description: The differential map d: A -> Ω_{A/B} satisfies (i) additivity: d(a)+d(a')=d(a+a'), (ii) Leibniz rule: d(aa') = a d(a') + a' d(a), and (iii) triviality on pullbacks: d(b)=0 for b in image of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the three basic properties that characterize differentials; they are the starting point for all constructions of the module/sheaf of relative differentials. (Caution: d is B-linear but not in general A-linear; see Exercise 21.2.A.)

rubrics_metrics.name: First (explicit) definition of Ω_{A/B}
rubrics_metrics.description: Ω_{A/B} is generated by formal symbols 'da' for a in A, subject to the three rules (additivity, Leibniz, triviality on pullbacks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete hands-on construction useful for computations and examples (e.g., for A = k[x,y], B = k one gets differentials like 3x^2 dy + 4 dx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key fact: generation by generators and relations
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is generated over B by elements x_i with relations r_j, then Ω_{A/B} is generated by the d x_i subject to the relations d r_j = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You only need a generating set of A and generators of relations to compute Ω; this underlies practical computations (see Exercise 21.2.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation / presentation of Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a finitely generated B-algebra then Ω_{A/B} is a finite type A-module; if A is finitely presented then Ω_{A/B} is finitely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the presentation A = B[x1,...,xn]/(r1,...,rj) to deduce finiteness properties. In Noetherian situations finite type and finitely presented coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior for quotients (vertical differentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A = B/I (quotient), then Ω_{A/B} = 0: da = 0 for all a in A because they come from B; intuitively there are no vertical cotangent vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: a closed immersion has no new 'vertical' directions coming from the base; see Example 21.2.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding free variables
rubrics_metrics.description: If A = B[x1,...,xn] then Ω_{A/B} = A dx1 ⊕ ... ⊕ A dxn (free module of rank n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches geometric intuition: cotangent bundle of affine n-space is trivial of rank n; applies even for infinitely many variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian description (cokernel of Jacobian matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = B[x1,...,xn]/(f1,...,fr), Ω_{A/B} can be written as (⊕_i A d x_i)/{d f_j = 0} and interpreted as the cokernel of the Jacobian matrix J: A^r -> A^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete method to compute Ω and to connect to the Zariski tangent space via linear algebra (see Exercise 21.2.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization behavior of Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a multiplicative subset of B and A = T^{-1}B (localization), then Ω_{A/B} = 0. More generally, pullback of differentials under localization gives isomorphisms (Exercises 21.2.L and 21.2.K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: localization corresponds to an open subset (no new vertical directions). The stronger statement: formation of Ω commutes with appropriate localizations/base changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field extension behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/k is a separable algebraic extension then Ω_{K/k} = 0; in characteristic p there are examples (e.g., K = k(t^p) inside L = k(t)) where Ω_{L/K} ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 21.2.F and 21.2.M investigate separability, transcendence bases, and freeness results for Ω in field extensions; use the relative cotangent sequence in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cotangent exact sequence (affine and global)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ring maps C -> B -> A there is a natural exact sequence A ⊗_B Ω_{B/C} -> Ω_{A/C} -> Ω_{A/B} -> 0 (Theorem 21.2.9), globalizing to morphisms of schemes as π^* Ω_{Y/Z} -> Ω_{X/Z} -> Ω_{X/Y} -> 0 (Theorem 21.2.25(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric meaning: tangent space to a fiber injects into total tangent space, cokernel is pullback of tangent space of base; expect left-exactness under smoothness (Exercise 21.2.S).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence (affine and global)
rubrics_metrics.description: For B a C-algebra with ideal I and A = B/I there is an exact sequence I/I^2 -> Ω_{B/C} ⊗_B A -> Ω_{A/C} -> 0 (Theorem 21.2.12), globalizing to closed embeddings i: X -> Y as N^∨_{X/Y} -> i^* Ω_{Y/Z} -> Ω_{X/Z} -> 0 (Theorem 21.2.25(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: dualizing gives normal/conormal bundles and explains how embedded subvarieties contribute to differentials; in smooth situations the sequence can be left-exact as well (see 21.2.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of conormal and normal sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed embedding i: X -> Y cut out by ideal sheaf I, define the conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y} := I/I^2 (viewed as a quasicoherent sheaf on X), and the normal sheaf N_{X/Y} := Hom(N^∨_{X/Y}, O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: I/I^2 generalizes the classical conormal space m/m^2; normal sheaf is its dual. Beware: dualizing twice need not recover the original module unless reflexive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular embedding implies locally free conormal/normal sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is generated by a regular sequence x1,...,xr (Noetherian A) then γ: (A/I)^⊕r -> I/I^2 sending (a1,...,ar) to Σ a_i x_i is an isomorphism, so I/I^2 is free of rank r and the conormal (and normal) sheaves are locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In codimension r regular embeddings the conormal/normal sheaves are vector bundles; for Cartier divisors (codimension 1) the conormal is O(-D)|_D and normal is O(D)|_D (Exercise 21.2.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal property of Ω (derivations representability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ω_{A/B} with the universal derivation d: A -> Ω_{A/B} represents B-linear derivations: for any A-module M, Hom_A(Ω_{A/B}, M) ≅ Der_B(A, M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterizes Ω up to unique isomorphism and is the conceptual reason for uniqueness and functoriality; use it to construct maps or prove identities (Section 21.2.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber of Ω at a rational point equals cotangent space
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a k-algebra and m ⊂ B a maximal ideal with residue field k, then Ω_{B/k} ⊗_B k ≅ (m/m^2)^∨ (Proposition 21.2.18): the fiber of Ω is the cotangent space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dualizing gives an isomorphism between Hom_k(Ω ⊗ k, k) and Hom_k(m/m^2,k), relating derivations to tangent vectors; this ties the algebraic Ω to classical Zariski tangent space computations (Jacobian).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global definition via diagonal (sheaf version)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X -> Y define Ω_{X/Y} as the conormal sheaf of the diagonal embedding Δ: X -> X ×_Y X; the universal derivation d on open U is given by d f = pr2^* f - pr1^* f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sheaf-theoretic definition glues the affine constructions and yields a global d: O_X -> Ω_{X/Y}; it aligns with the tangent-normal intuition via the normal bundle of the diagonal (Section 21.2.20–21.2.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local freeness for smooth morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X -> Y is smooth of relative dimension n then Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of rank n (Exercise 21.2.Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies Ω with the (dual of the) relative tangent bundle in smooth situations; many exact sequences become short exact sequences in this context (see remarks on left-exactness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of Ω under finiteness hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X -> Y is locally of finite type and Y (hence X) is locally Noetherian, then Ω_{X/Y} is a coherent sheaf on X (Exercise 21.2.P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives desirable finiteness properties for Ω in standard algebraic geometry contexts; hypotheses can be weakened for weaker conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback and base-change compatibility of Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative square X' -> X over Y' -> Y there is a natural map μ^* Ω_{X/Y} -> Ω_{X'/Y'}; if the square is Cartesian (X' ≅ X ×_Y Y') this map is an isomorphism (Theorem 21.2.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formation of Ω commutes with base change in Cartesian squares; use Exercise 21.2.K and 21.2.T for the affine reductions and gluing argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness of cotangent sequences under smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the relative cotangent and conormal sequences are generally right-exact, they become left-exact under appropriate smoothness hypotheses (see Remark 21.2.10, 21.2.13 and Exercise 21.2.S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition and Andrè-Quillen homology explain the missing left terms; in smooth situations the first homology vanishes yielding exactness on the left.
